summary: Defines new BGP-LS TLVs to carry the IGP Traffic Engineering Metric Extensions defined for IS-IS and OSPF. This lets a controller learn link performance data, such as delay, through BGP. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Routers measure how fast their links are. This lets them pass those measurements to a central planner using a messaging channel they already have.

questions: what are bgp-ls tlv code points 1114 to 1120
how does bgp-ls carry link delay
subtitle: Seven new BGP-LS attributes that carry link delay, loss and bandwidth measurements to a controller.

tldr.problem: IS-IS and OSPF can advertise link performance measurements, but BGP-LS had no way to carry them to systems outside the IGP.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines seven new BGP-LS Link Attribute TLVs, with code points 1114 to 1120, for delay, min/max delay, delay variation, loss, and residual, available and utilized bandwidth.
tldr.outcome: BGP-LS can now distribute the IGP Traffic Engineering Metric Extensions. IANA has assigned the seven code points.

today: RFC 8571 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2019. The unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
BGP - Link State (BGP-LS), defined in RFC 7752, defines NLRI and attributes for carrying link-state information in BGP. To carry the Traffic Engineering Metric Extensions of RFC 8570 (IS-IS) and RFC 7471 (OSPF), new BGP-LS Link Attribute TLVs are needed. This document defines them.

A TLV is a type, length, value record. The semantics and values of the fields inside each new TLV are not redefined here; they are described in RFC 8570 and RFC 7471.
sections.eli5: Routers already have a way to tell a planner about their links. This adds new kinds of notes to that channel, such as how fast and how full a link is.

sections.title: The Seven Link Attribute TLVs
sections.content:
Each TLV describes a measurement between two directly connected IGP link-state neighbors, and each follows the TLV rules of RFC 7752. The new TLVs are:

  • Unidirectional Link Delay (1114): the average link delay.
  • Min/Max Unidirectional Link Delay (1115): the minimum and maximum delay values.
  • Unidirectional Delay Variation (1116): the average delay variation.
  • Unidirectional Link Loss (1117): loss as a packet percentage.
  • Unidirectional Residual Bandwidth (1118).
  • Unidirectional Available Bandwidth (1119).
  • Unidirectional Utilized Bandwidth (1120): the bandwidth utilization.

The delay TLV has a Type of 1114 and a Length of 4. Its value has an A bit, a reserved field and a Delay field. The Min/Max TLV has Length 8 and carries both a Min Delay and a Max Delay. The delay variation, loss and bandwidth TLVs each have Length 4.
sections.eli5: There is one labeled box for each thing a router can measure about a link: how long it takes, how much it wobbles, how much gets lost, and how much room is left.

sections.title: Mapping to IGP Sub-TLVs
sections.content: Each new BGP-LS TLV corresponds to an advertisement sourced by the IGPs. For OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 these are defined in RFC 7471; for IS-IS they are defined in RFC 8570. For example, Unidirectional Link Delay is IS-IS sub-TLV 33 and OSPF sub-TLV 27. The table in the RFC runs from IS-IS sub-TLVs 33 to 39 and OSPF sub-TLVs 27 to 33, in the same order as the TLV list.
sections.eli5: Each new box matches a box that routers already use at home, so the number just gets copied into the shared channel.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The procedures and extensions do not affect the BGP security model. The RFC points to RFC 4271, RFC 4272 and RFC 6952 for BGP security, and to RFC 7752 for BGP-LS information.

The TLVs represent the state and resource availability of the IGP link. It is assumed that the IGP instances originating them support the security and authentication mechanisms of RFC 8570 and RFC 7471. Advertising this information presents no additional risk beyond the link attribute information already supported in RFC 7752.
sections.eli5: Sharing these numbers is no riskier than sharing what the channel already carries, as long as the routers that make them are protected.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA has made assignments in the 'BGP-LS Node Descriptor, Link Descriptor, Prefix Descriptor, and Attribute TLVs' registry for the seven new Link Attribute TLVs, using code points 1114 through 1120 as listed in the RFC.
sections.eli5: An official list of box numbers was updated so that everyone uses the same number for the same kind of box.
